summary: Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan ran again against Democrat Mary Peltola, a former U.S. representative. No winner has been declared yet because no candidate had a majority of first-choice votes, so a ranked-choice count is scheduled for Nov. 18.

candidates.name: Mary Peltola
candidates.bio: Mary Peltola is a Democratic former U.S. representative who won Alaska's only House seat in a 2022 special election and a full term that November, becoming the first Alaska Native member of Congress. She lost re-election in 2024 to Nick Begich III in the final ranked-choice round. She grew up fishing on the Kuskokwim River, lives in Bethel, and served in the Alaska House from 1999 to 2009.

positions.summary: Says Alaskans face scarcity and high prices and that systemic change is needed to bring down grocery costs.
Said in October 2026 that her immediate priority is reversing the damage to Medicaid.
Describes herself as pro-choice and said in 2024 she supports no restrictions on birth control and in vitro fertilization.
Said in 2022 that Alaskans are living with the devastating effects of climate change, and says she supports responsible resource development with local control.
Said in 2022 that quality schools are vital to the future of communities.

candidates.name: Dan Sullivan
candidates.bio: Dan Sullivan is a Republican U.S. senator from Alaska, sworn in January 6, 2015. He sits on the Commerce, Armed Services, Environment and Public Works, and Veterans' Affairs committees. He is a retired Marine Corps Reserve colonel with 30 years of service and previously served as Alaska attorney general and natural resources commissioner. He earned an economics degree from Harvard and a law degree from Georgetown.

positions.summary: Says he helped pass the biggest tax cut in American history.
Said in October 2026 that 'Obamacare destroyed the health care system here,' and supported repealing the Affordable Care Act in 2020.
Says the best way to lower energy costs is to produce more Alaskan energy by and for Alaskans.
Said in 2020 he supported shifting military funding to build a border wall, and said in 2014 that the border should be secured and that President Obama should not give 'executive amnesty'.
Said in 2020 he supports banning abortion after 20 weeks, and in 2014 that he supports an exception to protect the life of the mother.

factCheckNote: Confirmed uncalled by AP-syndicated reports and a Nov 14 tally: Peltola leads by about 10,400 votes with just under 50% of first choices; ranked-choice tabulation scheduled Nov 18.
